questions.question_text: Depreciation is:
options: The permanent and gradual decrease in the value of a fixed asset due to use, time or obsolescence
A temporary fall in market value
questions.explanation: The cost of the asset is spread over its life.

questions.question_text: Under AS 6, depreciation is a measure of:
options: The wearing out, consumption or other loss of value of a depreciable asset
questions.explanation: Arising from use, effluxion of time or obsolescence.

questions.question_text: A feature of depreciation is that it:
options: Is a non-cash charge spread over the asset's useful life

questions.question_text: Land is not depreciated because:
options: It generally has an unlimited life and does not wear out
questions.explanation: Its value normally does not decline through use.

questions.question_text: Depreciation is:
questions.explanation: No cash leaves the business when it is charged.

questions.question_text: Scrap (residual) value is:
options: The estimated value of an asset at the end of its useful life
questions.explanation: It is estimated at the time of purchase.

questions.question_text: Useful life is:
options: The period over which an asset is expected to be used by the business
questions.explanation: It may be shorter than its physical life.

questions.question_text: The depreciable amount is:
questions.explanation: The amount to be written off.

questions.question_text: Book value (written down value) is:
The cost of an asset for depreciation includes:
options: Purchase price plus freight, installation and other costs to bring it into use
questions.explanation: All costs incurred to make it ready for use.

questions.question_text: Depletion is:
options: Fall in the value of patents
The exhaustion of a natural resource by extraction, e.g., a mine

questions.question_text: Amortisation is:
options: The writing off of an intangible asset over its useful life, e.g., patents

questions.question_text: Fluctuation differs from depreciation in that fluctuation is:
options: A temporary change in market value and is not recorded in the books

questions.question_text: Obsolescence means:
options: Loss of usefulness of an asset because of new technology or changes in demand
questions.explanation: The asset becomes out of date.

questions.question_text: Depreciation applies to tangible fixed assets, depletion to _____, and amortisation to _____:
questions.explanation: Each term is for a different type of asset.

questions.question_text: Depreciation is necessary to:
options: Ascertain the true profit and show assets at a fair value

questions.question_text: Depreciation relates to the matching concept because it:
options: Allocates the cost of the asset to the periods benefiting from its use

questions.question_text: Depreciation:
options: Does not itself provide funds, but retaining profit equal to it conserves funds for replacement

questions.question_text: Causes of depreciation include:
options: Wear and tear, efflux of time, obsolescence, exhaustion and accident

questions.question_text: Wear and tear as a cause means:
options: The decline in value because of use of the asset

questions.question_text: Efflux of time as a cause means:
options: Value falls with the passage of time even if the asset is not used

questions.question_text: Obsolescence as a cause means:
options: Loss of value due to changes in technology or fashion
questions.explanation: A newer model makes the asset out of date.

questions.question_text: Exhaustion as a cause means:
options: The asset's contents are used up, e.g., mines and quarries

questions.question_text: Accident as a cause means:
options: Sudden loss of value through fire, flood or breakdown

questions.question_text: Factors affecting the amount of depreciation include:
options: Cost, estimated scrap value and estimated useful life

questions.question_text: The straight line method charges:
options: An equal amount every year = (Cost − scrap) ÷ life
questions.explanation: The rate on cost is constant.

questions.question_text: The WDV method charges depreciation:
options: At a fixed percentage on the book value each year

questions.question_text: A merit of the straight line method is that it is:
options: Simple and can write off the asset to scrap value

questions.question_text: A demerit of the straight line method is that it:
options: Writes off the asset too fast
Ignores the fact that repair costs rise as the asset ages, making the total charge uneven
questions.explanation: Total charge (depreciation + repairs) is higher in later years.

questions.question_text: A merit of the WDV method is that it:
options: Charges more in early years when the asset is most efficient and evens out depreciation plus repairs

questions.question_text: A demerit of the WDV method is that it:
options: Never writes the asset off to zero and is more complex
Writes the asset off to zero

questions.question_text: SLM is suitable for assets like:
options: Patents, leases and buildings, which lose value evenly over time

questions.question_text: WDV is suitable for assets like:
options: Machinery and vehicles with rising repairs and rapid early fall in value
questions.explanation: Their efficiency is highest in early years.

questions.question_text: SLM differs from WDV in that SLM charges depreciation on:
options: Original cost (equal amounts), WDV on book value (declining amounts)
questions.explanation: SLM gives a straight line; WDV gives a declining charge.

questions.question_text: The WDV method never writes off an asset to zero because:
options: Depreciation is a percentage of a reducing balance, which never reaches zero

questions.question_text: The total charge (depreciation + repairs) is more even under WDV because:
The sum of years' digits method charges:
options: A decreasing amount each year based on the remaining life over the sum of the digits

questions.question_text: The units of production method charges depreciation based on:
options: The number of units produced or hours used

questions.question_text: The annuity method treats the asset's cost as:
options: An investment earning interest, with depreciation computed so that the interest and depreciation total a fixed annuity
questions.explanation: Interest on the investment is also considered.

questions.question_text: The depreciation fund method:
options: Sets aside an amount each year and invests it to buy a replacement asset
questions.explanation: Also called the sinking fund method.

questions.question_text: The insurance policy method:
options: Takes a policy to provide funds for replacing the asset
questions.explanation: The premium is paid each year.

questions.question_text: The revaluation method:
options: Values the asset at the end of the year, and the fall in value is depreciation
questions.explanation: It is used for small items like livestock and loose tools.

questions.question_text: The rate of depreciation under SLM is:
questions.explanation: It is a percentage of cost.

Method 1 of charging depreciation:
options: Debit Depreciation A/c, credit Asset A/c (asset shown at reduced value)
questions.explanation: The asset account is reduced directly.

questions.question_text: Method 2 of charging depreciation:
options: Debit Depreciation A/c, credit Provision for Depreciation A/c (asset shown at cost)
questions.explanation: The asset remains at original cost.

questions.question_text: Under the provision method, the asset is shown in the balance sheet:
options: At cost less accumulated provision for depreciation

questions.question_text: Method 1 differs from method 2 in that in method 1 the asset account is:
options: Credited directly, while method 2 keeps it at cost and credits a provision account

The effect of depreciation on the balance sheet is that it:
options: Reduces the book value of fixed assets

questions.question_text: Depreciation affects tax because:
options: It is an allowable deduction that reduces taxable profit

questions.question_text: A change in the method of depreciation is allowed:
options: Only when required by law or when it gives a more appropriate presentation

questions.question_text: A change of method is accounted for by:
options: Recalculating depreciation under the new method from the date of use and adjusting the difference

questions.question_text: Schedule II of the Companies Act, 2013 specifies:
options: The useful lives of assets for depreciation

questions.question_text: Under Schedule II, useful lives are specified for:
options: Buildings, plant and machinery, computers and other assets

questions.question_text: Under Schedule II, the residual value is generally not more than:
A block of assets for income tax depreciation is:
options: A group of assets with the same rate of depreciation, treated together
questions.explanation: Depreciation is calculated on the block's WDV.

questions.question_text: Ind AS 16 deals with:
questions.explanation: It covers recognition, measurement and depreciation.

questions.question_text: The cost model carries an asset at:
options: Cost less accumulated depreciation, while the revaluation model uses fair value
questions.explanation: The revaluation model needs regular revaluations.

questions.question_text: Depreciation begins when:
options: The asset is available for use

questions.question_text: The useful life should be reviewed:
options: At least at the end of each financial year

questions.question_text: Depreciation differs from repairs in that depreciation is:
options: A gradual write-off of the cost of an asset, whereas repairs maintain the asset's efficiency

questions.question_text: Depreciation is also called a provision for replacement because:
options: It spreads the cost so that profits are retained to replace the asset
questions.explanation: It does not provide cash by itself.

questions.question_text: Ignoring depreciation:
options: Overstates profit and the book value of assets, and hence capital
questions.explanation: The accounts do not show a true position.

questions.question_text: A machine costs Rs 1,00,000; depreciation 20% for 3 years: the charge under SLM is _____ each year, and under WDV the charge in year 1 is:
questions.explanation: WDV charges fall in later years (20,000, 16,000, 12,800).

questions.question_text: Under the cost concept, inflation causes depreciation to be:
options: Understated relative to the replacement cost of the asset
questions.explanation: Funds are insufficient to replace the asset.

questions.question_text: For a leased asset:
options: The lessee depreciates a finance-leased asset, while an operating lease is not depreciated by the lessee

questions.question_text: In a year with a loss, depreciation is:
options: Still charged, as it is not dependent on profit
questions.explanation: It is a charge irrespective of profit.

questions.question_text: Depreciation differs from a sinking fund in that depreciation is:
options: A write-off of the asset's cost, while a sinking fund is a cash investment to replace the asset
questions.explanation: The sinking fund method combines both.

To charge depreciation of Rs 10,000 under the provision method:
options: Depreciation A/c Dr to Provision for Depreciation A/c, then P&L A/c Dr to Depreciation A/c
questions.explanation: The depreciation account is closed to P&L.
